gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the whole-kit weight (station plus the panels in the box) or Wh per lb. On those numbers, the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W kit (2,073.6 Wh, 87.7 lb, 23.6 Wh/lb, $0.72/Wh) carries 80% more battery than the AC180 + 2×200 W kit (1,152 Wh, 69.6 lb, 16.6 Wh/lb, $1.07/Wh). It costs $267 more, weighs 18.1 lb more and has the same 400 W of panels. Anker's C2000 Gen 2 + PS400 Bifacial is the lightest kit for its capacity at 32.2 Wh/lb.
standout_why: I compared against Lights On Labs (cited in 3 chats), StormWatts 'same panel watts' (cited twice) and RuntimeMath 'Sun Hours to Full'. All three already give cost per Wh and hours or days of sun to refill. StormWatts covers 24 kits with a 4.5 sun-hour, 0.85-efficiency model, so refill time is already taken. None of them gives any kit weight, so none can give Wh per lb or carry weight with the panels included. None gives a measured usable Wh figure either. Our own current page has no weight column and no derived columns.
decides: For a 'panels included' buyer who will carry the kit, total weight with panels changes the 2 kWh pick. The Anker C2000 Gen 2 + one 400 W bifacial panel is 63.6 lb for 2,048 Wh (32.2 Wh/lb). The Elite 200 V2 + 2×200 W is 87.7 lb for 2,073.6 Wh (23.6 Wh/lb), so it is 24 lb heavier for the same panel watts. Among the BLUETTI kits, a second 200 W panel halves full-sun refill time but costs portability. AC180 + 1×200 W is 52.5 lb (22.0 Wh/lb, $0.67/Wh); adding the second panel takes it to 69.6 lb (16.6 Wh/lb, $1.07/Wh). At 400 W of panels, the Elite 200 V2 kit is the better buy than the AC180 kit on cost per Wh, and it weighs 18.1 lb more. This confirms the 2 kWh class over the 1 kWh class once the buyer pays for 400 W of panels.
